inputs.text: This account treats security as Israel’s freedom to keep using force and asks the US to hold firm, while casting Iran’s demands as coercion. That framing leaves out the central question: whether a ceasefire can protect civilians and reduce the risk of further violence, rather than preserve one side’s military options. The Strait of Hormuz matters, but invoking its security should not become a blanket excuse to reject negotiation or impose terms through US pressure. A durable settlement needs to address the power imbalance and protect people on all sides—not just reassure governments that they can keep escalating.
